articleTitle: System evolution: a useful insight into strategic change
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on a Systems Approach to Manufacturing
abstract: The paper reports the use of systems methods in the management of change. It is based on experiences in a number of companies although the principal points are illustrated by reference to the industrial diamond industry. This summary contains: (a) propositions which the author believes are sustainable and represent conclusions to date, and (b) case material.

articleTitle: A holonic approach to CIM architecture and systems design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on a Systems Approach to Manufacturing
abstract: The paper presents an improved solution to the design of computer integrated manufacturing (CIM) systems. This is based on an innovative systems architecture to support a holistic approach, focused on meeting customer need. The real life complexity of the manufacturing enterprise is recognised and dealt with in a manner that is both simpler and at the same time more comprehensive than traditional methods. It encompasses people, organisation, information, technology, computer based systems and business processes.

articleTitle: A systems approach to process improvement in design and manufacture
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on a Systems Approach to Manufacturing
abstract: The desirable state for a systems engineering firm to be in is to adopt the tenets of concurrent engineering (CE), a means for accomplishing this desired state is to use the doctrine of business process reengineering supported by a suitable systems approach. The ideas postulated in the paper give a new angle of approach to concurrent engineering, as it has been viewed from a human centred stance and reinforced by system models that can visually demonstrate concurrency or lack of it. This approach can help employees at all levels understand what is going on around them, therefore stimulating reengineering actions for improving any concurrency.
